source.com: Project 2021 through scripts/oracle_lock.py on neutral copies under (C:/w29/g1-14/zoom-size/). Three copies of tests/data/synthetic-base.mpp differ only in the applied view's +1180 u16 (control 0x0064 = 100; 0x0006 = 6; 0x0106 = 262). Each was opened, its TimescaleStart/Finish read at window width 966 pt, read again after a resize, and closed. Probe: build/w29/zoom_size_probe.py; output: (C:/w29/g1-14/zoom-size/zoom_size.json).

stored_project_a.other_views: every other 41363-byte Gantt view record stores +1181 = 0; several store exactly 14400 (1984-01-01), which is Project's stock default and not a saved scroll position

stock_default.meaning: no saved scroll; the port must not pin the axis to it, or a 2026 plan would render thousands of empty days before its first bar

encoding.start: tenths of a minute since 1983-12-31 00:00; 14400 units per day; date32 day 0 is also 1983-12-31, so the conversion is a split at 14400
encoding.size: u16 percentage. MPXJ reads only the low byte and would report 6 for PROJECT_A; Project 2021 renders the stored 0x0106 as 262 % (see com_controls)

capture.chart_pane_note: the white drawing area ends at x = 1897; the last ~12 px sit under the vertical scrollbar and are still part of the timescale width

visible_range.note: the capture's own later scroll, 90 days right of the stored 2025-12-01 origin; the stored origin, not this range, is what the port applies

capture.day_width_note: each column width divided by its calendar day count, averaged over the ten complete months: 102/31, 98/30, 102/31, 99/30, 102/31, 102/31, 98/30, 102/31, 99/30, 102/31 = 3.2875. The axis is calendar-day continuous, so 31-day months are 102 px and 30-day months 98-99 px.
capture.pane_cross_check: 1028 px / 312.6 days = 3.289 px/day, the same value within a pixel

window.note: same window, same sheet columns and same chart pane in every variant (its boundaries are +/-1 px; the width ratios, not the absolute px/day, are the claim); the only difference is the applied view's +1180 u16

com_controls.conclusion: 262 renders 2.625x the control's width at the same window, so Project reads +1180 as a u16 and not as its low byte. Reading the low byte alone (6) would be 16.7x narrower than 100; Project instead clamps the narrowest rendered day column to about 2 px, which is the 12x-wider 006 observation, so that variant is evidence for the high byte and not for a linear 6 % rule.

pan_zoom_field_writes.PanZoomZoomTo: writes +1176 and +1180, never +1181; a one-day zoom saved size 181 with a minutes bottom tier

mapping.day_base_source: tests/data/reference/wave25-auto.measures.json: day_width_px 24.0 for the stock view, size 100, days bottom tier
mapping.axis: the percentage scales the BOTTOM TIER's unit column, not a fixed day: a days tier at 100 % is 24 px/day, a months tier at 100 % is 38.2 px/month. PROJECT_A stores months, so its 262 % gives ~100 px/month = 3.288 px/day. The port draws a calendar-day axis and paints the stored year/quarter/month tiers from their own units, keeping month columns proportional.

notes: No screenshot of a client file is committed; only these numbers are.
PROJECT_A is never opened in place; its fields were read from a neutral copy.
The port's reader decodes +1180 as a u16 and +1176 as a u32; tests/viewstate_tests.cpp patches 06 01 into a stock blob and expects 262.

The stored 262 % with a months tier is the only PROJECT_A zoom case. Weeks, quarters, years, hours and multi-count tiers have no measured 100 % column width and are left at the shell zoom (the origin still applies).
